definitions.explanation: A small, affordable paperback book in the standard Japanese bunko format (approximately A6 size, 105 × 148 mm). A distinctive feature of the Japanese publishing industry, bunko editions are typically reprints of hardcover books released at a lower price point.

examples.japanese: {文庫本|ぶんこぼん}なら{鞄|かばん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: A paperback will fit in a bag.

examples.japanese: ハードカバー⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{文庫本|ぶんこぼん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧ことにした。
examples.english: Since the hardcover is expensive, I decided to wait until the paperback comes out.

examples.japanese: ⟦{通勤|つうきん}{電車|でんしゃ}→通勤電車：08568_tsuukindensha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{文庫本|ぶんこぼん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んでいる→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}かける→見かける：01644_mikakeru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: You often see people reading paperbacks on commuter trains.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of ⟦{文庫|ぶんこ}→文庫：18437_bunko⟧ (library/collection) and {本|ほん} (book). The bunko format is a staple of Japanese publishing — major publishers have their own bunko lines (e.g., {新潮文庫|しんちょうぶんこ}, {角川文庫|かどかわぶんこ}). Bunko books are typically priced around ¥500-800, significantly cheaper than hardcovers. They are popular for reading on trains due to their compact size.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {文庫本|ぶんこぼん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧: to read a paperback
- {文庫本|ぶんこぼん}⟦{化|か}→〜化：28335_ka⟧: publication in paperback format
- {文庫本|ぶんこぼん}⟦サイズ→サイズ：01363_saizu⟧: paperback size

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{単行本|たんこうぼん}→単行本：11937_tankoubon⟧: standalone book, hardcover edition
- ⟦{新書|しんしょ}→新書：16406_shinsho⟧: shinsho (a slightly taller pocket-sized nonfiction format)
